questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
Language as communication is crucial in my field of study. 
Financing options as living abroad isn't a cheap experience.
Reputation - The quality of the University - so to speak - as the quality of my education concerns me. 
Location, as I like to spend my days off out and about exploring, whether it be nature or cultural treasures.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I personally need more clear communication as a lot of the clinics I went to, had no idea that I was coming, even though I wrote them a few days before each time. This was due to the fact that the person "responsible" for me often was on vacation or out sick, and no one else knew I was coming or had any idea were I should go or do.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Easy enough, helped with the office in the city.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: besides a key to my room, nothing

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: The "Student-housing" was 'first come, first serve' so that was easy enough. But I think if you get into the right WhatsApp-groups finding housing there is also easy enough.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: transportation takes longer, but it's like it always is living off campus?

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I got the message that I had to accept my room quick, so that other students could benefit if I wasn't interested and that "Under no circumstances it is possible to change the dormitory room or the dormitory itself!.." and I had to rent it for the hole semester, only to find out that a lot of their rooms are empty and it would be almost impossible to find a new tenant. Also I moved in to the dirtiest 4-person flat and was told when I moved out that it had to be totally clean "like when I got it", so not only did I have to fight not to have to pay 3 months extra rent, I also had to clean YEARS of dirt including fridges and bathrooms that weren't even mine....

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did a clinical stay, so no idea

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I wrote my coordinator what was needed from my University and what clinics I would like to do, and she organized it with the hospital.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The coordinator

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: 3 out of 3

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't do cardiology, do something else for internmedicin

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Clinical stay

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: there wasn't any.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Clinical stay - surgery - 5 weeks
Clinical stay - internal medicin - 5 weeks
Anesthesiology - 2 weeks

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Orthopedic surgery as it gives you practical skills and probably nephrology or urology as internal, as the patient group is wider.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Sports for the student by the students at sportscience and the students did a lot of cross-cultural dinners

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Sportcard, as its an easy and fun way to get some exercise and meet people.
Stamm-tisch to meet exchange students. 
Finding people from your own country because sometimes it's nice to be whit "your own people" in your own language.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Explore the region, it's full of beautiful citys and forrests.
Your also close to France, Austria and Luxembourg, so go. 
Nice museums in Frankfurt.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quit easy as im not that far from home, but more southern than I'm used to.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Didn't meet many as I only did the clinical stay.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: They are closed people, they're not looking for new friends, so you really have to prove yourself worthy.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The kindness and the mix of culture.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. You're not staying for long, so live somewhere nice.
2. Try to find energy to do the social things so you meet new people.
3. Remember to plan more time for moving there and back, so you don't pressure yourself.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Studenthousing isn't necessary the best option even though it's cheap.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Improving my 3th language and get to be a part of the proces in the clinic

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Language-barrier in the beginning.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
